name: cc-enforcer
description: Rules your coding agent physically cannot ignore. A Claude Code plugin (and LLM-agnostic rule pack) that stops reactive patching, guessed citations, surface-level fixes and premature "done" claims by intercepting the agent's own tool calls — PreToolUse denies the edit before it lands, and a nine-layer Stop gate refuses to let a completion claim end the turn without evidence, a convergence self-quiz, a fidelity check against the original request, and a one-line TL;DR. Twelve rules, eight of them backed by a hook; per-project "Imperial Edict" regexes you define yourself; a repo-wide sync gate; CI drift gates that derive every documented number from the code so the docs cannot rot. Zero dependencies, stdlib only, and every guard fails OPEN — a bug in the discipline can never brick your agent. v0.37.0 fixes the boundary every hook invocation goes through: each entry point read its payload with `sys.stdin.read()`, which decodes using the HOST codepage under the `surrogateescape` error handler, so on any non-UTF-8 machine the JSON arrived silently rewritten and every guard scanned a string the agent never wrote — no exception, no stderr, no failing test. Measured on cp936, an em-dash arrived as two characters instead of one, which pushed an inline note past the rule-09 rationale floor and turned a DENY into an ALLOW: the guard was defeated by punctuation. The Stop gate had far more to lose — `大白话`, `同步核对`, `我觉得` and the done-claim patterns themselves are Chinese, so they decoded to mojibake and the CJK half of nine layers matched nothing in production. `_has_done_claim` gates all nine layers and its pattern set is bilingual, so a reply announcing completion only in Chinese matched nothing and skipped the whole stack — measured, a bare completion claim with no evidence came back allowed with not one layer having fired. Stated precisely rather than loosely, because the looser version would be the overstatement this plugin exists to block: a reply that also said "done" in ASCII still reached layer (a); what it could not do was fail on a Chinese hedge, a Chinese TL;DR marker, or a Chinese sync-check line. Same class as the v0.25 `tomlio` hardening (a wrong decode silently disabling enforcement), swept twelve releases late to the one boundary that carries every payload. Fixed at the mechanism with a new shared module, `lib/hookio.py`: read the binary buffer, decode UTF-8 strictly, and let a genuinely malformed payload raise into the existing fail-open handler — loud and diagnosable instead of quietly mangled. It survived 691 tests because the fixtures could not reach it: `tests/_helpers.py` serialised with `json.dumps`, whose `ensure_ascii=True` default escaped every non-ASCII character before the bytes existed, so the wire was pure ASCII and the decode step had nothing to get wrong. The harness now sends raw UTF-8 and a test pins that it does; the end-to-end cases force `PYTHONIOENCODING=cp936:surrogateescape` so a defect that only appears on a non-UTF-8 host still fails on the UTF-8 CI runner, with a vacuity guard that reports a stale reproduction rather than a fixed bug. Five cases verified RED against the pre-fix tree. 691 -> 712 tests. Prior — v0.36.0 adds a demo you can run: the same task, twice, against identical starting files, with the hooks as the only variable. A payment module raises KeyError when the gateway declines — loud, and pointing at the line that caused it. Without the plugin, five reactive edits all land: the crash is swallowed into a `None`, the suite goes red, and a sign-off claiming it is green ends the turn with nothing checking the claim. With the plugin, three of the five are refused (the swallow, the fourth small patch, and the evidence-free sign-off), and the run is pushed into one systematic rewrite that names the root cause. The point is the LAGGING error: patching a loud failure does not remove it, it makes it quiet — a stack trace becomes a ledger holding rows the gateway refused, and nothing reports it until someone reconciles a statement weeks later. Both transcripts render to terminal SVGs embedded in the READMEs. Every cc-enforcer verdict in them is verbatim hook stdout; every test and probe result is captured from a real run; the agent's five moves are scripted, which is stated plainly because a demo that overstated itself would be the exact defect this plugin exists to catch. tests/test_demo.py re-runs the demo and compares byte for byte, and — because equality alone would be satisfied by a demo that stopped denying anything — also asserts each verdict by content and asserts the unguarded run still ends in a silent failure. 682 -> 690 tests, then 691 in v0.36.1, which fixed the demo images: they were rendered on Windows, so the deny banner carried a backslash-joined path that Linux reproduces with a forward slash, and a byte-for-byte pinned artefact may not contain a platform-dependent string. Fixed at the mechanism and asserted by its own test. Full release history: CHANGELOG.md.
